history.summary: The Shree Pahadeswar Temple, better known locally as the Pahadi Mandir, stands on top of a small hill on the eastern side of Jharsuguda town, Jharsuguda district, Odisha. Lord Shiva is worshipped here. The temple was constructed in 1921 by Gujarati contractor Lt. Bitthal Bhai Saha, and the hilltop complex also has a garden and an ashram, making it a popular picnic spot as well as a place of worship. From the hilltop there is a bird's-eye view of Jharsuguda town. The Jharsuguda district administration lists it 3 km from the railway station and 3.5 km from the bus stand, with the nearest airport at Jharsuguda itself. CSV town 'Jharsuguda' is correct; no correction needed.

name: Shree Pahadeswar Temple
town_description: Jharsuguda is a town and the district headquarters of Jharsuguda district in western Odisha. It is an important railway junction (South Eastern Railway, on the Tatanagar-Bilaspur section of the Howrah-Nagpur-Mumbai line) and has its own airport (Veer Surendra Sai Airport) about 9 km from the city. Nearby attractions include the Pahadi Mandir hill, Jhadeswar Temple, Kali Mandir and the Koilighughar waterfall.
